title: US Bancorp Deep Dive Analysis
summary: Bank funding, duration and fiscal-regime resilience.
assessment: The report correctly anticipated renewed Treasury purchases and a near-term Bitcoin high. Its bank framework usefully joins funding vulnerability with duration exposure, but overstates some historical claims and blurs NIM, leverage and goodwill accounting. USB performed well; peers and underlying explanations had mixed outcomes.

claims.claim: Banks received broader crisis bailouts than homeowners.
claims.reason: The article contrasts rapid bank recapitalization with homeowner losses, and later qualifies the comparison with “mostly.” That broad asymmetry is not refuted by the existence of assistance. Its earlier categorical wording is too strong: HAMP, announced in 2009, supported mortgage modification and foreclosure prevention. Mortgage assistance is also different from recapitalizing a household or making every borrower whole.

evidence.title: Home Affordable Modification Program
evidence.finding: Public and private efforts provided mortgage assistance to nearly five million Americans.

evidence.title: Making Home Affordable program update
evidence.finding: The administration announced the housing program in February 2009; detailed HAMP guidelines followed in March.

claims.direction_assessment: Comparative asymmetry is plausible; a categorical absence of homeowner support is inaccurate.
claims.timing_assessment: Distinguish the immediate 2008 bank response from housing programs launched in 2009.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Bank recapitalization and mortgage modification use different mechanisms and reach different populations.

claims.claim: A new Fed chair will be more accommodative.
claims.reason: The successor’s September 2026 rate hike is adverse evidence for a simple easing expectation. It does not establish how Powell would have responded to the same conditions, or settle the new chair’s full term. “More accommodative” is a relative disposition without a fixed endpoint, so a single hike cannot cleanly falsify it. Yield-curve steepening and reserve expansion remain separate propositions.

Bank leverage is usually assets relative to loss-absorbing capital; reserve abundance and leverage can move independently.
